posts.author: Thunder-FN
posts.body: Hello, I'm a newbie here and I would like to know if there is a way to avoid autotiles for mapping in MZ. The tilesets I am using for the ground and water animations do not have the MV/MZ arrangement, to be more specific my ground tiles are 3x3 blocks instead of 2x2 and my water animations are 4 frames instead out of 3. I saw that there is a plugin to be able to map from TileD but I have never used TileD and I don't know if that tool can solve my problem.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Have you tried using MZ? Done tutorials with it?
There's an entire A sheet - everything on that sheet is considered ground, and the last portion of it is not autotiles. Additionally, you can use MZ's manual layer selection to choose any tile on any sheet and place it on the ground layer.
It sounds like you're using something that
is
an autotile, if it's more than just 1 tile, but configured for a different maker.
How much trouble you have converting that to RPG Maker will depend entirely on your understanding of RPG Maker's behavior and your skills with an image editor.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Thunder-FN said:
And my main doubt is how viable it is to make maps without using A-1 to A-4 sheets?.
Click to expand...
There is no need to use autotiles in MZ at all, they just make a lot of things easier.
Without autotiles you are limited to B-E tiles, which means you have less tiles available in your tileset. But if you can get all the needed tiles into the B to E slots of regular tiles, then you can use them on a map without problems.
The second difficulty is that you'll probably have to use manual layering. The automated layering places A tiles into the bottom layer and the B-E tiles into the two top layers. So for most cases you need to manually place your ground B-E tiles into the bottom layer.
but as long as you keep those two restrictions in mind, there should be no problem making a map without using A# sheets.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
The portions of that which are analogous to RPG Maker autotiles aren't in 3x3 chunks, they're in 4x4 areas.
You can certainly use this as a learning and practice experience, but frankly if you're not comfortable with basic image editor usage to copy and paste portions of a gridded area, you're probably better off not buying things that aren't already formatted for RPG Maker.
But, as Andar said (and I said in my first reply), by using other sheets and the layer system, you don't have to use
any
autotiles. It just gets increasingly tedious.

Be aware that Parallax maps can use a LOT of memory if they're too big. Keep your maps small. If you are exporting template maps from RMMZ to get a basis for your parallax work in your image editing software (like photoshop or gimp), RMMZ will half the size if you export a template too large. (It's very annoying).
I'm fairly new to RMMZ, but I'm pretty good at making nice looking maps. I found I had to split large levels into different screens. I opted to pretty much scrap the idea of having a world map. That's just my experience (heads up).
